text:
Hi, I’m Noor Halden, a Python developer with 6 years of experience building production systems and ML-powered applications.

I’d be a strong fit for your ecommerce platform because my background combines backend development, machine learning, and practical work with Python-based APIs and background jobs. In recent projects, I built a support ticket triage model for Kettlewell Support Co. using Python, scikit-learn, FastAPI, Celery, Redis, and PostgreSQL. The system routed incoming helpdesk tickets to 14 queues, and it improved macro-F1 to 0.88 from 0.62 with the old keyword rules while reducing median routing time from 6 hours to 4 minutes. I also built a contract clause search assistant using Python, LangChain, OpenAI API, pgvector, PostgreSQL, and FastAPI. It answered questions over 9,000 contracts and always quoted the clause and page it used, reaching 0.91 faithfulness on a 120-question lawyer-written test set and cutting clause lookup from 25 minutes to 3 minutes.

Your stack of Django, Django REST Framework, and Celery is closely aligned with the kind of Python backend work I’ve done, and I’m comfortable working on systems that need to stay reliable while scaling. I also have experience with machine learning, including scikit-learn, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, XGBoost, pandas, NLP, LangChain, and the OpenAI API, so I can contribute on both the application and AI sides of the product. I’m used to collaborating with distributed teams, clarifying task specifications, and also working independently when a problem needs focused attention.

I’d be glad to help maintain the current application, improve the backend architecture, and support growth as the product expands to more products, customers, and features. Since your platform involves large-scale ecommerce data and AI-driven product identification, I’d be especially interested in how your Django services are currently organized around data access, background processing, and the AI layer.

What parts of the Django app are the most urgent right now: scaling the current product catalog workload, improving existing APIs, or adding new functionality?
